Usage: hashiru <command> [args]

Commands:
  update [stage ...]   Pull the latest Hashiru, then run install.sh.
                       Stage selectors are passed straight through, so
                       'hashiru update 45' re-applies only config and
                       'hashiru update 45+' runs stage 45 onward.
  install [stage ...]  Run install.sh WITHOUT pulling. For iterating on local
                       changes — 'update' refuses on a dirty checkout.
  doctor [--json]      Read-only health check (never modifies the system).
                       --json prints one JSON document for scripts.
  config               Edit this machine's hashiru.conf in $EDITOR, seeding it
                       from hashiru.conf.example the first time. Aliased as
                       'edit'. Machine-local *config* — monitors, kitty, waybar
                       — lives beside it in ~/.config/hashiru/.
  fingerprint [on|off [--forget]]
                       Fingerprint for sudo and polkit prompts. 'on' checks
                       for a reader, enrolls a finger if none is, and turns it
                       on; 'off' turns it off and keeps the prints for
                       hyprlock, unless --forget. Bare, shows where it stands.
                       A failed scan always falls back to the password.
  charge [START STOP|off]
                       Battery charge thresholds: start charging below START
                       percent, stop at STOP (e.g. 'hashiru charge 75 80'), kept
                       across updates. 'off' goes back to the factory 0/100.
                       Bare, shows what's set and what the battery reports.
  status [--porcelain] Show install provenance, checkout state, and whether a
                       pull is available. --porcelain prints stable key=value
                       lines for scripts.
  tui                  The system menu, hashiru-tui (also SUPER+ALT+Space).
  version              One line: the version this machine is running.
  log [-f|--last]      Page the install log; -f follows it live, --last shows
                       only the most recent run.
  report               Warnings from the last install, if there were any.
  changelog [tag]      Release notes, newest first, or just one tag's.
  help                 This message.

Stage selectors match install.sh: N, N+, --from N, or several at once.
'hashiru install --list' names every stage; anything else install.sh accepts
works through 'install' too, since that is a straight passthrough.

Flags (accepted by both 'update' and 'install', passed to install.sh):
  --no-confirm         Answer every prompt with yes. The only prompt a run has
                       left is the reboot at the end, so on a full run this
                       does reboot — pair it with --no-reboot if you'd rather
                       it didn't. Package transactions were already
                       non-interactive (pacman and yay run --noconfirm).
  --no-reboot          Never reboot and never ask. Wins over --no-confirm.
  --no-reflector       Skip stage 10's mirror ranking, worth about a minute.
                       reflector.timer has been re-ranking weekly since this
                       machine was built, so on an update the ranking buys
                       nothing; the timer stays enabled either way.

All three are per-machine settings too — HASHIRU_ASSUME_YES, HASHIRU_NO_REBOOT
and HASHIRU_NO_REFLECTOR in hashiru.conf ('hashiru config'). A flag raises its
knob for one run; leaving the flag off does not lower a configured one. To drop
one for a single run, set it in the environment: HASHIRU_NO_REBOOT=0 hashiru
update.

No flag touches the dirty-checkout refusal or the sudo password prompt:
the first is a hard error rather than a question, and the second can't be
answered with a "y". For a genuinely unattended update, warm the sudo
timestamp first ('sudo -v') or give the user NOPASSWD.

Repo: /opt/hashiru
